audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both call this an "Even matchup — difficulty 6/10", which contradicts diff:"HARD", the 47.01% Emerald+ win rate over 2476 games, and the packet level chart (Aatrox favoured in 6 of 7 rows).
audit.why: Aatrox is a lane bully into a champion with no early sustain but passive regen. Mundo concedes early, mid and side-lane trades and only wins once HP stacking flips the attrition war. 47.01% is a losing lane, not an even one.
audit.corrected: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Aatrox carry threat 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three level charts disagree. content win[3..5] and full phases[3..5].side hand Levels 4-5 to "Skill" and Level 6 / First item to Dr. Mundo, but the packet levelChart, the whys[] prose and the win rate all say Aatrox owns everything up to two items.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage (R, 120s flat) heals missing health and gives move speed, but World Ender gives Aatrox attack damage, increased healing and move speed and extends on a takedown — the amped drain out-paces the one-shot heal in a straight brawl. Mundo's only genuine spike is the second HP item, when Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal and his health-scaled Blunt Force finally out-grind Aatrox's lifesteal. whys[3] ("Still his"), whys[4] ("so 6 is Aatrox") and whys[5] ("keeping the edge Aatrox") already say this; only the enum tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5, Level 6 and First item all flip to Aatrox (4/10); 2+ items stays Dr. Mundo (7/10). Chart flips proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions (report[5].t) contained no interaction at all — just "track World Ender, anti-heal and out-scale it". The decisive kit interaction of the matchup was absent from every field. Separately, whys[4] and spikes[1].text both claim World Ender has a "revive": Riot's text is "gaining attack damage, increased healing, and Move Speed. If he gets a takedown, this effect is extended" — there is no revive in the current World Ender.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases (P) resists the FIRST immobilising effect that hits Mundo, costing him health and dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and cut the passive's cooldown. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W, 20/18/16/14/12s) drag and his third Darkin Blade swing are both immobilises, so the first one Aatrox lands is eaten by the cannister and the second is the real one. Heart Zapper (W, 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s) stores damage Mundo takes and pays a percentage back as healing on the burst, so Aatrox's own damage partly funds Mundo — which is why both sides are in a Grievous Wounds race. Umbral Dash (E, 9/8/7/6/5s) carries both his escape and his passive lifesteal on champion damage. Infected Bonesaw (Q, 4s) stops on the first enemy hit, so Aatrox body-blocks it with the minion line. Deathbringer Stance (P) is an auto-attack reset that heals off max health — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell. Mirror (aatrox__drmundo) states the same facts from the other side.
audit.corrected: Goes Where He Pleases eats his first immobilise — Infernal Chains or Q3 pops the cannister, so walk it up to heal, then dodge the second.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all carry a PDF scrape artifact: "• • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 85". The trading rule itself was also vague ("line up your trajectory cleanly past enemy minion models").
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw stops on the first enemy hit, so the real rule is to throw it when Aatrox steps out of the wave, not to line up a trajectory. Blunt Force (E) is an auto-attack reset, so the trade is auto into E, then leave before the third Darkin Blade swing.
audit.corrected: See edits — artifact removed, replaced with the actual Q-block rule, the E auto-reset and the cannister disengage.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed only World Ender and quoted it as a flat 100s. Riot's per-rank cooldown is 120/100/80.
audit.why: Umbral Dash (9/8/7/6/5s) is the punishable cooldown in lane — it is his only escape from a Mundo E and R walk-down.
audit.corrected: World Ender quoted as 120/100/80s; Umbral Dash (9s) added as the step-up window.

audit.why: Nothing in the brief indicates a 26.15 change to either kit. Not asserting a patch claim without a source.

notes: REAL FABRICATION KILLED: whys[4] and spikes[1].text both claimed World Ender has a "revive". It does not — Riot's text is AD, increased healing, move speed, minion fear, and a takedown extension. The packet's suspectNames hit on "World Ender's" was a FALSE POSITIVE (just the possessive); the actual error was the revive claim next to it. CHART CONTRADICTION: content win[3..5] and full phases[3..5].side disagreed with the packet levelChart, with the whys[] prose in the same file, and with the 47.01% win rate. Flipped Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item to Aatrox as one atomic group so all three charts and the prose agree. PDF SCRAPE ARTIFACT: "• • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 85" was embedded in tradeGood, breakdown.trading and report[3].t — removed in all three and the space reused for the real Q-block, E-reset and cannister rules. Aatrox W carries a "grounding" derived flag that Riot's own text does not support (the text describes a drag back to centre); I did not assert grounding anywhere. Aatrox Q3 knock-up is not in Riot's tooltip text either but is stated by the already-written mirror audit, so I kept it consistent rather than contradicting the mirror.
